claims.claim: In the 1982 Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth the dungeon areas carry boxed text while the wilderness areas do not.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: while the dungeon areas use boxed text, the wilderness does not
claims.page: section '1982 - Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth Publication'

claims.claim: Gygax's 1974 Castle Greyhawk notes gave a single curt bullet-line per encounter area.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: only a single curt bullet-line per encounter area

claims.claim: Gygax's 1976 Lost Caverns of Tsojconth tournament document moved from bullet points to full English sentences describing each area.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: here we at least get full English sentences describing each area
claims.page: section '1976 - Lost Caverns of Tsojconth Tournament'

claims.claim: In the 1978 Steading of the Hill Giant Chief the area paragraphs tend to lead with sense-descriptions.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: the paragraphs tend to lead with those sense-descriptions
claims.page: section '1978 - Steading of the Hill Giant Chief'

claims.claim: Expedition to the Barrier Peaks devotes almost 500 words to the Ship Commander's Quarters, an area with no monsters.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: almost 500 words total for the one area
claims.page: section '1980 - Expedition to the Barrier Peaks'

claims.claim: Isle of the Ape opens with a boxed speech by Tenser of some 1,600 words to be read verbatim.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: 2 full pages of text to be read verbatim
claims.page: section '1984 (c.) - Dungeonland & Temple of Elemental Evil'

claims.claim: The Temple of Elemental Evil's introductory boxed text runs about 1,300 words, more than a full page.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: introductory boxed text section that runs more than a full page
claims.page: section '1984 (c.) - Dungeonland & Temple of Elemental Evil'

claims.claim: Delta counts 1,200 words of content text for room 404 of the Temple of Elemental Evil, a 20 by 30 foot room.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: room 404 is ironically a 20'×30' room with 1,200 words
claims.page: section '1984 (c.) - Dungeonland & Temple of Elemental Evil'

claims.claim: The Temple of Elemental Evil tends to open an encounter with non-boxed information for the DM before the boxed description.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: start with some non-boxed info to the DM, and then
claims.page: section '1984 (c.) - Dungeonland & Temple of Elemental Evil'

claims.claim: Delta locates in the 1982 Tsojcanth the moment monster stat blocks grew too big to sit inside the paragraph text.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: monster stat blocks grew too big to comfortably fit within the paragraph
claims.page: section '1982 - Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth Publication'

claims.claim: Delta says boxing his own sensory lead-in would imply reading it verbatim, which he calls a bad idea for a volatile situation.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), comment reply on 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: that seems to imply the need to read it verbatim

claims.claim: A reader argues boxed text is linear and assumes the characters approach a room from one specific direction.
claims.source: Warren D., reader comment on Delta's D&D Hotspot, 2021
claims.quote: because it is linear, it often assumes PCs are approaching the room

claims.claim: A reader praises Old-School Essentials room descriptions that bold the important object and put details in parentheses.
claims.source: Warren D., reader comment on Delta's D&D Hotspot, 2021
claims.quote: Room descriptions have important object in bold with parenthesis containing details

claims.claim: In the 1979 Lost Tamoachan the initial area descriptions are set as quoted and indented passages rather than boxed text.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Tip-Offs in Tamoachan', Delta's D&D Hotspot, 2017
claims.quote: not exactly in boxed text, but in specially quoted and indented

claims.claim: Bruce Cordell wrote that the 4e tactical format makes a compelling adventure narrative difficult to generate.
claims.source: Bruce Cordell, Design & Development column (2011), quoted by Mike Bridges, Greyhawkery
claims.quote: The tactical format makes it difficult to generate a compelling adventure narrative
